correctness.rationale: The exact neighbor-majority inequalities force all row supports to be nested, hence each equilibrium has a unique Ferrers shape. Necessary/sufficient corner inequalities classify every Ferrers row; the explicit extension E bijects size \(n-1\) shapes to n shapes with a zero row and the complement-transpose involution exchanges this family with the positive-last-row shapes, proving the \(2^n\) class law inductively. Equal-row and equal-column stabilizers give the factorial labelled formula. Direct exhaustive tests of 66,064 matrices (\(n=2,3,4\)), all Ferrers partitions through \(n=8\), and two implementations of stability predicates confirm the calculations. No finite sampling supports the infinite inference.

value.rationale: The natural square rook graph is a canonical Cartesian product and bipartite line graph. The fixed-state geometry and exact count of inequivalent equilibria are meaningful dynamical invariants and furnish a complete all-size classification, not a chosen finite slice or routine numerical computation. The doubling bijection explains the nonobvious \(2^n\) law; the stabilizer formula permits all labelled counts. The result claims neither new information at isolated n=4 nor attractor-basin theorems.
